instructions.content: Keep plugins as orchestration tools, not business-logic containers.
Prefer small, composable generation steps over large mutation passes.
Keep executors deterministic and cache-aware.
Use Tree API exclusively for filesystem operations in generators.
Create the plugin structure with npx create-nx-plugin for a new workspace, or npx nx add @nx/plugin then npx nx g plugin for an existing one.
Define a typed schema with required fields for generator options.
Add generator templates with EJS syntax.
Validate generators with --dry-run before execution and before broad rollouts; stop if unexpected files appear or required options fail validation.
Return { success: boolean } from the executor function.
Use package notation for executor references in targets.
Declare outputs for cacheable tasks.
Run plugin tests with nx test and validate the generator and target in a real workspace.
NEVER modify files outside the Tree API.
NEVER hardcode project paths in generator logic; derive them from readProjectConfiguration(...).root.
NEVER skip schema validation and typed options.
NEVER generate across project boundaries without explicit checks; verify tags and dependency direction and respect existing tags.
NEVER mutate project configuration blindly; read, modify and update rather than overwriting project.json.
NEVER put business logic directly inside executor entrypoints.
NEVER use relative executor references in targets.
NEVER omit outputs and dependencies semantics for cacheable work.
NEVER block executor runs with synchronous file I/O in hot paths.
NEVER skip formatFiles after generating code.
NEVER ignore existing project structure when generating files; check tree.exists before writing.
NEVER forget to export the generator or executor from the plugin index and register it in generators.json.
When directory is omitted use the workspace default location, and apply safe schema defaults for omitted optional flags.
